{{short description|Expresses Eisenstein series as a weighted average of theta series of lattices in a genus}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Siegel–Weil formula''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Weil|authorlink=André Weil|year1=1964|year2=1965}} as an extension of the results of {{harvs|txt|last=Siegel|authorlink=Carl Ludwig Siegel|year1=1951|year2=1952}},  expresses an [[Eisenstein series]] as a [[weighted average]] of [[Theta function of a lattice|theta series]] of lattices in a [[Genus of a quadratic form|genus]], where the weights are proportional to the inverse of the order of the [[automorphism group]] of the lattice.
For the constant terms this is essentially the [[Smith–Minkowski–Siegel mass formula]].
